newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Tuesday on profit-taking after registering new 1997 highs for three straight sessions up to Monday, brokers said.
The correction today was sparked by concerns over poor 1996 annual results, which are expected to flood the market ahead of the April 30 deadline, they said.
The B share index dipped 3.40 points or 1.87 percent to end at 178.39 on turnover of HK$199.4 million against Monday's HK$368.4 million.
"Caution is likely to characterise the market later this week as the remaining B share firms are expected to publish weak 1996 results," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
"Most of the good B share companies have published their results and the market is possibly facing some poorly performing companies," the analyst said.
Of the 20 B share companies yet to make public their 1996 results, most posted weak 1996 interim and 1995 annual earnings, analysts said.
"But the impact of poor results is likely to be small because investors have digested it and are looking ahead to their 1997 results," the analyst said.
Analysts said listed companies are expected to benefit in 1997 from the two interest rate cuts in 1996.
The market is now poised to move higher and break the 200-point level after today's correction, analysts said.
"Even at 200 points, the B shares are still not overpriced compared with their A share equivalents, a trader with Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"The recent bull-run has gained the attention of foreign investors and I expect a fresh injection of funds," the Guotai analyst said.
Television maker Shenzhen Konka was the biggest B share loser, sliding HK$0.63 or 5.34 percent to HK$11.17 on volume of 1.07 million shares due to profit-taking.
Wafangdian Bearing was the most actively traded share, slipping HK$0.11 to HK$6.94. on volume of 3.57 million shares. The stock had risen nearly 40 percent over the past few sessions.
The A share index rose 1.69 points or 0.36 percent to finish at 473.19 on turnover of 10.6 billion yuan.
